info.name: ABC Pharmacy API
info.description:
# ABC Pharmacy REST API

Every endpoint the Ionic app uses, with assertions on the status code, the shared response envelope and the documented error codes.

## Running it

1. Import this collection **and** `abc_Pharmacy.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the **ABC Pharmacy** environment and fill in `clientId` and `clientSecret` from Setup > External Client App Manager > abc_Ionic_App > Settings > OAuth Settings > Consumer Key and Secret.
3. Run the folders in order: **0. Setup**, **1. Authentication**, **2. Products**, **3. Carts**, **4. Error cases** - or just run the whole collection, which does the same thing.

Authentication is handled once: **1. Authentication** stores the bearer token and the instance URL as collection variables, and every other request inherits them.

The requests depend on the demo data created by `scripts/apex/abc_seed_data.apex`.

Full reference: `docs/API_DOCUMENTATION.md`.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description:
Run this first. It exchanges the External Client App's consumer key and secret for an access token using the OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow, then stores the token and the instance URL as collection variables so every other request picks them up automatically.

Set `clientId` and `clientSecret` in the environment before running.

exec: pm.test("Response carries an access token", function () {

request.description:
Must go to the org's My Domain host, not login.salesforce.com.

Client credentials authenticates the application, not a person. A production Ionic app should use Authorization Code with PKCE so each customer acts as themselves; this flow is used here to keep a reviewer's setup to one call.

item.name: 3. Carts
item.description:
The cart lifecycle. A cart is a Draft order, so checkout activates the same record rather than copying it into a new one.

Run these in order: the create request stores `cartId` for the rest.

item.name: 4. Error cases
item.description:
Every documented failure, one request each. These are what the Ionic app has to handle, so they are part of the contract as much as the happy path.

Each one also writes an abc_Log__c row in Salesforce carrying the same requestId the response returns.
